subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should the remaining Discord `messages` gate be split into read, edit, and delete permissions while send stays outside it, and how should existing booleans map to the granular defaults?
rationale: The missing least-privilege capability is source-proven, but selecting permanent defaults and compatibility semantics for destructive operations requires maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Granular read/edit/delete
options.body: Keep send outside the gate and support `messages: boolean | { read?: boolean; edit?: boolean; delete?: boolean }`, with omitted fields inheriting the boolean or existing default.

options.title: Separate top-level gates
options.body: Add independent read, edit, and delete action keys with an explicit doctor migration or deprecation path for the released `messages` key.

options.title: Keep remaining coarse gate
options.body: Retain one shared permission for fetch, read, edit, and delete and document selective denial as unsupported.

recommendation.title: Granular read/edit/delete
recommendation.body: Keep send outside the gate and support `messages: boolean | { read?: boolean; edit?: boolean; delete?: boolean }`, with omitted fields inheriting the boolean or existing default.

likelyOwner.reason: Gustavo authored the refactors that currently define both Discord action discovery and runtime enforcement, making him the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
